summary: Code review PASS. All six files reviewed against the TypeScript originals and against the WP acceptance criteria. The CJS port is clean, idiomatic, self-contained, and matches the design intent of the original TypeScript source. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: index.js — Module structure is excellent. 'use strict' at the top, JSDoc on every exported symbol, clear section comments, and a factory-pattern entry point (ledgerPlugin) that is composable and side-effect-free. The renderedOutputCache Map closure is correctly scoped per plugin instance, preventing any cross-instance state leakage.

index.js — onBuildContext defensively emits empty strings ('') for roster_rendered and mcp_tools_table on non-ledger personas. This prevents unresolved-variable WARNs in templates for those personas, which is the correct behaviour.
index.js — The composite cache key '${persona.name}:${target}' in onPostRender/onValidate is sound. Falls back to 'unknown' when target is undefined (unit-test contexts) — good defensive coding.

role-validator.js — escapeRegExp is correctly inlined with a comment referencing its origin (persona-builder src/utils/regex.ts). The implementation covers all standard RegExp special chars (.*+?^${}()|[\]). The validateRole function properly handles both Array and Set as manifestRoles input. The validateNoteOnlyGuard regex pattern | `toolName` | is precise and uses the inlined escapeRegExp for safety.

roster-renderer.js and mcp-tools-renderer.js — Both are minimal, pure functions with zero side effects. JSDoc examples are accurate and serve as lightweight executable specs. The note_only filter in mcp-tools-renderer.js correctly uses !t.note_only (coerces undefined to false, so entries without the flag are included by default).

frontmatter-templates.js — The CC_FRONTMATTER_FIELDS inline constant correctly mirrors the ccFrontmatterFields() helper. Template variable names match what the build context injects. The has_mcp conditional block for mcpServers is well-formed. No issues.

persona-build.config.js — require('./plugins/ledger') correctly resolves to the local CJS index.js. manifest.roles.map(r => r.name) passes the correct string array to ledgerPlugin. warnOnUnknownRole: true is explicitly set (safe default). No residual references to @mistralys/persona-builder (confirmed by grep across the entire plugins/ directory).

No security concerns. All modules are 'use strict', purely functional, no eval/Function constructor usage, no file I/O, and no dynamic require() calls. The escapeRegExp inline prevents ReDoS via user-supplied tool names.

Minor style observation (non-blocking): persona-build.config.js uses inconsistent spacing in the destructured require on line 19 compared to other requires in the file (some use padding spaces around braces, some do not). This is cosmetic only and does not affect functionality.
